channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Elon Musk Highlights Starlink's Role in Kazakh Tourists' Mountain Rescue
item.description: Elon Musk promoted Starlink after it facilitated the rescue of five Kazakh citizens stranded in the snowy mountains of East Kazakhstan. Their SUV broke down, leaving them without mobile service. Starlink's satellite internet enabled them to contact rescuers, who used the connection to locate and reach them.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Detains 38 Suspected Members of Hizb ut-Tahrir
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has detained 38 suspected members of the banned religious-extremist organization Hizb ut-Tahrir. The GKNB reported that most detainees held mid-to-high-level leadership positions. Evidence of radical ideology dissemination and recruitment was gathered.

item.title: Russia Reintroduces Fuel Purchase Limits at Gas Stations Amidst Infrastructure Attacks
item.description: Russian oil company Rosneft has reportedly reintroduced fuel purchase limits at its gas stations across dozens of regions. The restrictions, citing attacks on oil refining infrastructure, limit sales to 30 liters in urban areas and 50 liters on highways, with sales in canisters prohibited.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates IT Procurement Rules to Include 25% Developer Profit Margin
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development has updated its methodology for calculating costs for state IT projects. The new rules, effective November 10, now include a 25% profitability margin for IT developers. This aims to ensure fair compensation for companies developing digital solutions for government agencies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: "Kempirabad Defenders" Form Movement, Candidate Registration Nears End
item.description: Politician Adakhan Madumarov has endorsed former deputy Ishak Masaliev for the presidential election, as Masaliev's own candidacy was blocked due to a criminal record. Meanwhile, the "Kempirabad Defenders" have formed a United Democratic Movement, planning to nominate several candidates and calling for unity to restore democracy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Uzgen District Allocates Over 423 Million Som for Social Facilities in 2026
item.description: Uzgen District in Kyrgyzstan's Osh region has allocated 423.2 million som for the construction and repair of 28 social facilities in 2026. Seven projects, including schools, kindergartens, and a water supply system, have already been completed. The district also plans to build three more schools in 2027. Discussions also covered road reconstruction and socio-economic development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Gasoline and Diesel Exports Until May 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has extended the ban on exporting oil products to all countries. The order is effective from November 22, 2026, to May 22, 2027. The ban prohibits the export of gasoline, diesel, and certain other oil products via road transport, with exceptions for lubricants and fuel in vehicle tanks.

item.title: Afghan Refugees in Tajikistan Report Increased Fear of Detention and Extortion
item.description: Afghan refugees in Tajikistan are living in fear of arbitrary detention and extortion by security forces, even those with legal residency documents. Reports indicate a recent increase in detentions, with some refugees forced to pay large sums to avoid deportation. This situation makes daily life extremely difficult for the community.

item.title: Zhambyl Region Discusses Priorities from Head of State's Address
item.description: An information group met with residents in Taraz, Bayzak, and Zhambyl districts to explain the priorities outlined in the Head of State's address. Discussions focused on agricultural development, rational water resource management, irrigation system modernization, and support for farmers and rural entrepreneurship. Residents also shared proposals on social and infrastructure issues.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Awards State Prizes for Achievements
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov presented state awards to citizens who made significant contributions to major international and state events and achieved high results in their professional activities. He emphasized that these events strengthened Kyrgyzstan's international standing and showcased its organizational capabilities.

item.title: Expert: President's Address Signals Shift from Political Reform to Economic Development
item.description: An expert stated that the President's address outlined a transition from political reforms to a focus on economic development. The speech indicated a strategic shift in the nation's priorities, emphasizing economic growth and stability.

item.title: Karakalpakstan to Receive $100 Million for Infrastructure Renewal
item.description: Karakalpakstan plans a major upgrade of its social and utility infrastructure, allocating $100 million from a World Bank program and additional funds for schools, hospitals, and water facilities. This initiative aims to foster economic growth and improve living conditions.

item.title: Court Overturns Verdict in Fergana Kindergarten Poisoning Case; Company Head and Technologist Re-imprisoned
item.description: The Fergana Regional Court of Appeals has overturned a previous verdict concerning the mass poisoning of kindergarten children. The court re-sentenced the head and technologist of "Garden Catering Trade" LLC to 4 years and 3 years 6 months imprisonment, respectively, for violating sanitary laws and embezzlement.

item.title: Nurafshon Technology Center to Receive IT Park Benefits in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish a "Future Technologies Center" in Nurafshon, Tashkent region, offering companies within it the same tax and customs benefits as IT Park residents. These incentives include exemptions on profit tax, VAT, and customs duties for imported equipment until 2040.

item.title: Public Transport Fares to Increase in Astana
item.description: Public transport fares in Astana are set to increase from 110 to 150 tenge for non-cash payments starting mid-December. The city administration cited rising operational costs, including a threefold increase in fuel prices since 2014, and increased expenses for parts and maintenance. Discounts for vulnerable groups will be preserved.

item.title: Uzbek-Russian Partnership Achieves Concrete Results, Reaches Highest Level
item.description: Vadym Titov, head of a Russian Presidential Directorate, stated that Uzbek-Russian relations have reached their highest level, manifesting in concrete projects across trade, economy, energy, education, and culture. Bilateral trade has increased significantly, and numerous Uzbek students are studying in Russia, with 15 Russian university branches operating in Uzbekistan. Cultural exchange events are planned for the upcoming year.

item.title: SCAT flight from Moscow to Almaty diverted to Astana due to system indication
item.description: A SCAT Airlines flight en route from Moscow to Almaty made an unscheduled landing in Astana. The airline stated that a board system indication, signaling a potential technical issue, prompted the crew to divert to the base airport. Passengers reported an 'emergency landing' and lack of amenities, though the airline claims refreshments were provided.

item.title: Over 80% of Uzbek employers satisfied with university graduate preparedness
item.description: A national survey reveals that 86.8% of employers in Uzbekistan are satisfied with the preparedness of university graduates, while 65.1% are satisfied with vocational school graduates. Employers highlighted a need for more practical training and better interaction between educational institutions and businesses. Demand for AI and digital skills is growing.

item.title: Tajik Citizen Who Signed Contract with Russian Defense Ministry Dies in Ukraine War
item.description: A 53-year-old citizen of Tajikistan, Ziyoviddin Murodov, has died in the war in Ukraine. According to a relative, he signed a contract with the Russian Ministry of Defense about three months ago and voluntarily went to war due to debts. His wife is reportedly traveling to Russia to retrieve his body.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Naryn Industrial Park Plans Raise Electricity Supply Questions
item.description: Plans for a 200-hectare industrial park in Kyrgyzstan's Naryn Free Economic Zone, including data centers, face questions about electricity supply. The country already expects to import a significant amount of electricity and faces potential shortages during peak hours.

item.title: Family of teen who died in Ala-Archa appeals to Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov
item.description: The family of 14-year-old Amir Kunakunov, found dead in the Ala-Archa mountains, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov. They request a change in the pre-trial detention measure for his father, Maksat Kunakunov, citing pressure and threats of losing property. They also seek an objective investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Poverty Reduction Stalls Despite Economic Growth, World Bank Reports
item.description: Kazakhstan has shown minimal progress in poverty reduction recently, despite consistent economic growth, according to a World Bank brief. The national poverty rate remained at 5% in 2025. While earlier poverty reduction was driven by employment earnings, recent GDP growth has not translated into wage increases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Distribute 170 Tajik-Donated Homes to Border Conflict Victims
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing to distribute 170 houses, received from Tajikistan through territory exchange, to residents affected by border conflicts in the Batken region. Of the 213 houses transferred, 170 are deemed habitable. Priority will be given to those whose homes were destroyed in the 2021-2022 clashes.

item.title: Sunflower Oil Disappears from Markets Again in Turkmenistan Amidst Supply Issues
item.description: Sunflower oil has again become scarce in Mary province markets, with traders citing artificial difficulties and weak presidential directives on supply. Despite claims of ensuring food security, Turkmenistan faces persistent food issues, particularly with cooking oil, as reported by sources.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Rating System for Construction Companies
item.description: Kazakhstan will introduce a rating system for construction companies, allowing homebuyers to check a developer's past projects and legal disputes. The system, part of the Automated Register of Licensees, will be tested in November 2026 and fully operational by January 2027. Companies failing to meet requirements may face license suspension.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President: Kumtor Gold Mine to Operate Until 2050
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov announced that the Kumtor gold mine will continue operations until 2050, clarifying previous statements about the mine's closure. While the central open-pit mine's reserves will be depleted, extraction will continue using underground methods. Equipment will be repurposed for the Zhetim-Too deposit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks Scale in South Korean Investment for Alatau City Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to secure significant South Korean investment for Alatau City and K-PARK, despite existing "strategic partnerships" and memoranda. While Korean entities like KIND are involved in planning and concept development, actual foreign direct investment is still needed. Progress in initial stages should not be mistaken for achieved financial commitments.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Simplify Bank Guarantees for International Tender Participants
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch a separate platform within "Shaffof Qurilish" for energy sector projects with specific requirements. The government will also simplify the process for issuing bank guarantees for companies participating in international tenders. This aims to support enterprises with production experience and financial stability, reducing collateral requirements.

item.title: Russian Expert: Uzbekistan is a Model Partner for Digital Platforms
item.description: Fedor Lukyanov, editor-in-chief of 'Russia in Global Affairs,' views Uzbekistan as a model partner for Russian digital platforms. He noted the high organization of the Uzbek-Russian media forum and the mutual interest in developing cooperation. Lukyanov emphasized that media now extends beyond traditional journalism to shape daily life and business.

item.title: Illegal Stone Extraction Valued at 115 Million Tenge Discovered During Road Repair
item.description: During the capital repair of the Almaty-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway in the Zhetysu region, illegal extraction of stone and soil was discovered. The preliminary damage to the state is estimated to exceed 115 million tenge. A criminal case has been initiated for unauthorized subsoil use.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims for Full Mechanization of Cotton Harvest by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's authorities plan to completely transition to machine harvesting of cotton starting in 2027. This season, combines gathered 75-80% of the crop. The government intends to reallocate nearly 53,000 hectares unsuitable for large machinery to other crops. The Minister of Agriculture stated the goal is to eliminate manual cotton picking entirely.

item.title: Key Directions of President's Address Discussed in Ulytau Region
item.description: A meeting was held in the Ulytau region to explain the main directions of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the people, titled 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era.' Participants discussed priorities such as digital transformation, AI development, improving public welfare, and social infrastructure.

item.title: Elon Musk Highlights Starlink's Role in Rescuing Five Individuals in Kazakhstan
item.description: Elon Musk acknowledged Starlink's crucial role in a rescue operation in Kazakhstan where five individuals, stranded with a broken-down vehicle in the mountains, used the satellite internet to contact rescuers. The incident occurred in the Kurshim district of East Kazakhstan region.

item.title: Shrinking Caspian Sea Threatens Kazakhstan's Transport Route Ambitions, Expert Warns
item.description: Kazakhstan's plans for the Trans-Caspian transport route face environmental challenges due to the shrinking Caspian Sea, according to environmentalist Vadim Ni. He questioned the coordination of these plans, noting the Ministry of Ecology's recent involvement and the sea's declining water level.

item.title: Tajikistan and Saudi Arabia Sign Pharmaceutical Cooperation Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan and Saudi Arabia have signed a framework agreement to boost cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector. The deal between Tajik company SAFROSE and Saudi firm Gabas Trading Co. aims to develop trade and economic ties, according to the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Tajikistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Sign Fuel Supply and Mining Cooperation Agreements
item.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan have signed a framework agreement on fuel supplies and expanded cooperation in mining and manufacturing. The agreements were reached following talks between Presidents Tokayev and Rahmon in Astana, with businesses concluding deals worth $2.5 billion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Unified Register of Paid State and Municipal Services
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy has approved a unified register of paid state and municipal services, including civil law services. This document, based on a new law, details each service's name, administrator, provider, terms, payment, and outcome, aiming to inform citizens and businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Gas Safety Measures Ahead of Winter Season
item.description: Uzbekistan is intensifying preventive measures to ensure safe and economical natural gas usage for over 30,000 households in the Navoi region. Local gas supply departments are conducting awareness campaigns in communities, emphasizing the dangers of carbon monoxide, the importance of chimney maintenance, and proper installation of exhaust pipes. Residents are reminded not to use gas stoves for heating and to avoid homemade appliances.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $11.6 Billion Investment in Electrotechnical Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement 164 investment projects worth $11.6 billion in the electrotechnical and related industries over the next three years. The projects focus on electronic components, industrial robotics, cable manufacturing, transformers, pumps, transport and electromobile components, and household appliances. Responsible leaders and key customers will be assigned to each direction to attract investors and foster collaboration with research centers.

item.title: Ukraine Drone Strike Causes Fire at Russia's Second-Largest Oil Refinery
item.description: Ukraine launched drone attacks that caused a fire at Russia's second-largest oil refinery in Kirishi, near Saint Petersburg, on the night of November 9. The regional governor reported that the fire was contained, but one woman died from shrapnel injuries. Ukraine reportedly used 113 drones in the attack. The Kirishi refinery processes up to 20 million tons of crude oil annually and has been targeted previously.
